content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted and passes the quality checklist. **This is the first SDD gate — please review before we plan or write any code.**

**Artifacts**
- `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY`: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- `SPEC_FILE`: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- Checklist: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` — all items pass.

## What the spec says (in plain terms)

A personal app to **save, find, organize, and maintain bookmarks**. Four user journeys, prioritized:

- **P1 — Save a bookmark**: paste an address, get an auto-titled entry; invalid addresses are rejected.
- **P1 — Browse & find**: list everything; search by keyword across title/address/tags; open to navigate.
- **P2 — Organize with tags**: tag bookmarks, filter by tag, rename/remove tags.
- **P2 — Edit & delete**: correct details; delete with confirmation and undo.

It also covers edge cases (duplicate addresses, unreachable pages, large collections, empty states) and sets measurable targets (e.g. find a bookmark among 500 in under 10 seconds; zero data loss across restarts).

## Two scope decisions I want your call on

I picked sensible v1 defaults so we aren't blocked, but these meaningfully change the app, so I'd rather confirm them with you now:

### Q1: Who uses it?

| Option | Answer | Implications |
|--------|--------|--------------|
| A | Single user, one device (my default) | Simplest; no accounts or login; no cross-device sync |
| B | Single user, synced across devices | Adds sync + a hosting/account story |
| C | Multiple users with accounts | Adds sign-in, per-user data, sharing questions |

### Q2: How do bookmarks get in?

| Option | Answer | Implications |
|--------|--------|--------------|
| A | Manual entry / paste an address (my default) | Self-contained app; nothing to install in the browser |
| B | Also a browser extension / "share to app" capture | Adds a separate capture surface and its own scope |
| C | Also import existing browser bookmarks | Adds a one-time import flow and file-format handling |

## Your options at this gate

- **Approve as-is** (defaults Q1=A, Q2=A) → I proceed to `speckit-plan`.
- **Answer Q1/Q2 differently** (e.g. "Q1: B, Q2: A") → I update the spec, then plan.
- **Any other changes** to scope, requirements, or success criteria → tell me and I'll revise the spec.

Nothing gets planned or built until you approve. How would you like to proceed?
Yeah, that all sounds right to me. Single user on my own machine is fine, and pasting in an address is how I'd expect to add them. Go ahead with your defaults — approved.
relayed: Yeah, that all sounds right to me. Single user on my own machine is fine, and pasting in an address is how I'd expect to add them. Go ahead with your defaults — approved.

content:
No `after_plan` hooks. Phase 0/1 design is complete. **This is the second SDD gate — please review the plan before I generate the task breakdown.**

**Artifacts** (`specs/001-bookmark-manager/`)
- `plan.md` — implementation plan
- `research.md` — the decisions and what was rejected
- `data-model.md` — Bookmark, Tag, and their link
- `contracts/api.md` — the local API the UI talks to
- `quickstart.md` — how we'll validate it works end-to-end

## The plan in plain terms

**Shape**: a small app you run on your own machine and use in your browser at `localhost`. It has two parts working together:
- a lightweight **local server** — stores your data, checks addresses are valid, fetches page titles for you, and catches duplicates;
- a **browser page** — the actual list/search/tag interface you interact with.

Everything stays on your machine. No accounts, no sign-in, no hosting.

**Storage**: a single local database file. Easy to back up (copy one file), fast enough to search thousands of bookmarks in well under a second, and it enforces "no accidental duplicate of the same address."

**Why a server at all** (since you're local/single-user): two things a browser can't do on its own — reliably fetch a page's title (browsers block that across sites) and store/search thousands of records quickly. The server handles those; opening a bookmark still just hands off to your browser.

**Key behaviors it locks in**: auto-titling with fallback when a page is unreachable, invalid-address rejection with a clear message, duplicate warning ("open the existing one?"), tag rename/remove propagating everywhere, and delete-with-undo.

## A couple of choices worth your explicit nod

- **Runs in your browser at localhost** rather than as a standalone desktop app. Lighter to build; opening links is native to the browser anyway. (A desktop app was considered and rejected as heavier for a one-person tool.)
- **The stack is a normal web toolset** (TypeScript throughout). You won't interact with it directly, but it means "install, run one command, open the page."

## Your options at this gate

- **Approve** → I run `speckit-tasks` to break this into an ordered task list (still no code yet).
- **Change a decision** (e.g. "I'd rather it be a desktop app," or "skip undo," or "I do want import after all") → tell me, I'll update the plan (and spec if the behavior itself changes) and re-present.

How would you like to proceed?
Sounds good to me — runs in the browser at localhost is fine, and being able to back up by copying one file is a nice touch. Approved, go ahead and break it into tasks.

content:
No `after_tasks` hooks. Task breakdown is generated.

**Artifact**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md`

## Summary

- **Total tasks**: 41, in dependency order across 8 phases.
- **Per user story**: US1 Save = 7 · US2 Browse/Find = 6 · US3 Tags = 6 · US4 Edit/Delete+Undo = 5. Plus Setup (4), Foundational (5), Duplicate detection (3), Polish (5).
- **Tests included** (as the plan committed to): unit tests, per-endpoint integration tests, and one end-to-end save→find→open journey.

**Independent test per story** (so each is demonstrable on its own):
- **US1** — paste an address → it appears auto-titled; invalid input is rejected.
- **US2** — search narrows the list to matches; opening one navigates to the page; no-match shows guidance.
- **US3** — tag a bookmark, filter by tag; rename/remove propagates everywhere.
- **US4** — edits persist; delete asks to confirm, then undo restores.

**Parallel opportunities**: within a story the `[P]` test tasks run alongside each other; across stories, once US1 lands, US3 and US4 can proceed concurrently (separate service methods and UI components).

**Suggested MVP**: Phases 1–3 (through **US1**) — a usable product that saves and lists bookmarks with validation and auto-titling. Then layer US2 → US3 → US4 → duplicate handling → polish.

**Format check**: all 41 tasks use the required `- [ ] Txxx [P?] [Story?] description + file path` format.

## This is the last gate before code

Per our SDD workflow, `speckit-implement` will actually write the app against these tasks. Options:

- **Approve** → I start implementing, MVP-first (Setup → Foundational → US1), pausing at checkpoints so you can see it working.
- **Adjust** — e.g. reprioritize, drop a story from v1, or want a `speckit-analyze` consistency check across spec/plan/tasks first.

Want me to begin implementation?
Looks good — I like the MVP-first approach with checkpoints. Go ahead and start implementing.

content:
The MVP checkpoint is complete. Here's where we are.

## ✅ MVP delivered — User Story 1 (Save a bookmark)

I implemented **Phases 1–3** of the task list (T001–T016) and verified it running for real.

**What works right now**, confirmed by a live run of the app:
- The page loads at `localhost` with the bookmark UI.
- **Save a bookmark** by pasting an address → stored and listed, newest first.
- **Auto-title** — I saved `https://example.org` with no title and it fetched **"Example Domain"** from the live page (falls back to the address if a page is unreachable).
- **Invalid addresses rejected** with a clear message ("Enter a full web address starting with http://…").
- **Duplicate detection** already returns the existing bookmark (this was foundational to save correctness; the *UI prompt* for it is still a later task).
- **Empty-state guidance** instead of a blank screen.
- Data persists in a single local SQLite file — back up by copying `data/bookmarks.sqlite`.

**Verification**
- 14/14 automated tests pass (`npm test`): title derivation + fallback (unit), and create/list/validation/duplicate (integration).
- Web UI builds cleanly (`npm run build:web`).
- Full API exercised end-to-end via a running server.

**To run it yourself**: `npm start`, then open the printed `http://127.0.0.1:3000`.

## What's not built yet (by design)

Per our MVP-first plan, these remain as approved tasks:
- **US2** — search + open (Phase 4)
- **US3** — tags: filter/rename/remove UI (Phase 5)
- **US4** — edit + delete with undo (Phase 6)
- **Phase 7** — duplicate *UI* prompt (T035/T036) and **Phase 8** — polish/perf/README

Note: one small, deliberate divergence from the strict task order — I implemented duplicate detection in the save service now (T034's service logic) because saving needed it to behave correctly; its dedicated UI + test tasks stay in Phase 7.

## Your call for the next checkpoint

- **Continue to US2** (search & open) → next natural increment toward a genuinely useful tool.
- **See it in the browser first** — I can walk you through `npm start`, or capture a screenshot.
- **Adjust priorities** — e.g. jump to edit/delete, or something you noticed you want changed.

Since anything that changes *behavior* routes back through the spec, just tell me what you'd like and I'll either continue implementing against the current spec or update the spec first. How shall we proceed?
Nice, that all works the way I'd expect. Keep going with US2 — search and open is what makes it actually useful.

content:
US2 checkpoint is complete.

## ✅ User Story 2 delivered — Browse and find

Implemented **Phase 4** (T017–T022) against the approved spec.

**What's new and working:**
- **Keyword search** across title, address, *and* tag names — verified live: `react` → title match, `cooking` → address match, `backend` → tag match.
- **No-match handling** — a search that matches nothing returns empty and the UI shows a distinct "No matches" message (separate from the first-run empty state).
- **Open a bookmark** — list items are links that open the saved address in a new browser tab (FR-008); long titles/addresses truncate in the list.
- **Detail endpoint** `GET /api/bookmarks/:id` with full fields (404 when missing) — verified live.
- Search box in the UI with debounced server queries and a clear button.

**Verification:**
- **21/21 automated tests pass** (`npm test`): added 7 integration tests for search + detail.
- Search/detail exercised end-to-end against a running server (results shown above).
- UI rebuilds cleanly.

**One honest caveat — the E2E browser test:**
- I wrote the Playwright journey test (`tests/e2e/save-find-open.spec.ts`) as planned (T018).
- It **could not run in this sandbox**: launching Chromium fails because the environment is missing system libraries (`libglib-2.0.so.0`) and I don't have root to install them. This is an environment limitation, not a code problem.
- The journey it covers (save → search → open) *is* verified by the integration tests plus the live API run. On your own machine, `npx playwright install` (which also pulls the needed deps) will let it run.

## Where we are

- **Done:** US1 (save) + US2 (find/open) — the app is now a genuinely usable bookmark tool: save, search, open. 22 of 41 tasks complete.
- **Remaining (approved tasks):** US3 tags UI (Phase 5), US4 edit/delete+undo (Phase 6), Phase 7 duplicate-warning UI, Phase 8 polish (perf check, persistence check, README).

## Next checkpoint — your call

- **Continue to US3** (organize with tags) — next in priority order.
- **Or jump to US4** (edit/delete with undo) if that's more valuable to you now.
- **Or pause here** and I can write the README / do a persistence + performance check.

How would you like to proceed?
Great, search and open working is exactly what I wanted. Continue to US3 — tags next.

content:
US3 checkpoint is complete.

## ✅ User Story 3 delivered — Organize with tags

Implemented **Phase 5** (T023–T028) against the approved spec.

**What's new and working** (all verified live):
- **Tag a bookmark** — add tags inline on any bookmark, or remove a tag from just that bookmark.
- **Filter by tag** — clickable tag chips with live counts (`work 2`, `reading 2`); selecting one narrows the list. Combines with keyword search.
- **Rename a tag** — propagates to every bookmark carrying it; verified `reading → articles` kept its count of 2 and updated bookmark 1.
- **Case-insensitive merge** — renaming a tag onto an existing name (e.g. `js → JavaScript`) merges them into one.
- **Remove a tag** — deletes it from all bookmarks; verified removing `work` left bookmark 1 with just `[articles]`.

**Verification:**
- **30/30 automated tests pass** — added 9 integration tests (tag counts, rename propagation, merge, remove propagation, tag filtering, filter+search combo).
- **Typecheck clean** (`tsc --noEmit`) — also fixed some pre-existing test-only typing warnings along the way.
- Every tag endpoint exercised against a running server (output above).

**Note on scope:** the contract routes tag edits through `PATCH /api/bookmarks/:id`, so I implemented that endpoint now for the `tags` field only. US4 will extend the *same* endpoint to cover title/address/description — no rework, just additions.

## Where we are

- **Done:** US1 (save) + US2 (find/open) + US3 (tags) — **28 of 41 tasks**.
- **Remaining:** US4 edit/delete + undo (Phase 6), Phase 7 duplicate-warning UI, Phase 8 polish (persistence check, ~5k performance check, README).

*(Unchanged caveat: the Playwright E2E test is written but can't execute in this sandbox — missing OS browser libraries, no root. It'll run on your machine via `npx playwright install`.)*

## Next checkpoint — your call

- **Or jump to Phase 7/8** (duplicate-warning UI, then polish/README) if you'd rather round things off.

How would you like to proceed?
That's the tag behavior I'd hoped for — rename carrying across everything is handy. Continue to US4, edit and delete with undo.

content:
US4 checkpoint is complete — all four user stories are now built.

## ✅ User Story 4 delivered — Edit and delete with undo

Implemented **Phase 6** (T029–T033) against the approved spec.

**What's new and working** (all verified live):
- **Edit** a bookmark's title, address, and notes via an inline form; changes persist and bump the last-modified time (FR-011).
- **Address re-validation on edit** — changing to an invalid address is rejected (400); changing to an address another bookmark already uses is blocked as a duplicate (409); saving the same address unchanged is fine (no false self-duplicate).
- **Delete with confirmation** — a confirm step, then the bookmark drops out of all lists/search/filters (soft delete, FR-012).
- **Undo** — a toast offers immediate restore; the bookmark comes back with its tags intact (FR-013). Verified: deleted "New Title" restored with its `keep` tag.
- Nice correctness detail: a deleted bookmark's address is freed for re-saving, and undo refuses (409) if that address was taken in the meantime.

**Verification:**
- **40/40 automated tests pass** — added 6 edit tests + 4 delete/undo tests.
- **Typecheck clean**, UI builds cleanly.
- Full edit → invalid-edit → delete → undo cycle exercised against a running server (output above).

## Where we are — the app is feature-complete for the spec

**33 of 41 tasks done.** Every functional requirement (FR-001…FR-015) now has a working, tested implementation. Save, find/open, tags, and edit/delete-undo are all in.

**Remaining — Phase 7 & 8 (rounding off):**
- **T034–T036**: the duplicate-warning *UI* prompt with "open the existing one" (the server-side detection already works and is tested; this adds the front-end affordance + its E2E-style test).
- **T037–T041**: polish — persistence-across-restart check, ~5,000-bookmark performance check (SC-003), special-character handling, a full quickstart walkthrough, and a `README`.

*(Standing caveat: the Playwright browser E2E can't run in this sandbox — no root to install browser libs — but the test is written and will run on your machine.)*

## Next — your call

- **Finish Phase 7 + 8** (duplicate UI, then polish + README) to fully close out the task list.
- **Or stop here** — the app is fully usable and all spec behaviors are implemented and tested.

How would you like to proceed?
Great, edit and delete with undo all behave the way I'd want. Go ahead and finish Phase 7 and 8 — round it off with the duplicate prompt and polish.

content:
🎉 **All 41 tasks complete.** The Bookmark Manager is finished, built, and verified against the approved spec.

## ✅ Phase 7 & 8 delivered — duplicate prompt + polish

**Phase 7 — Duplicate handling (T034–T036):**
- The add form now shows a **duplicate prompt** offering to open the existing bookmark instead of creating a copy (server-side 409 detection was already in place).
- 3 dedicated duplicate tests: 409 + existing bookmark returned, no copy created; case/whitespace treated as same address; different paths treated as distinct.

**Phase 8 — Polish (T037–T041):**
- **Persistence across restart** — verified with a real two-process restart: 2 bookmarks before, 2 after (T037).
- **Performance at scale** — 5,000 bookmarks: keyword search and tag filter return in **3 ms**, list-all in 89 ms — far under the 1-second target SC-003 (T038).
- **Special-character / non-Latin** titles and tags preserved and searchable, plus URL-normalization tests (T039).
- **Quickstart walkthrough** — all six scenarios (V1–V6) pass end-to-end against a running server (T040).
- **README** with install/run, features, and the "back up by copying one file" note (T041).

## Final state

| | |
|---|---|
| **Tasks** | 41 / 41 complete |
| **Tests** | 50 passing (unit + integration), across 10 files |
| **Typecheck** | clean (`tsc --noEmit`) |
| **Build** | clean (`npm run build:web`) |
| **Requirements** | FR-001…FR-015 all implemented & tested |
| **Success criteria** | SC-001…SC-006 met (SC-003 verified at 5k scale) |

**To run it:** `npm install` → `npm start` → open the printed `http://127.0.0.1:3000`.

## Two honest caveats (unchanged)

1. **Playwright E2E** — the browser journey test is written (`tests/e2e/save-find-open.spec.ts`) but **can't execute in this sandbox**: launching Chromium fails on missing OS libraries and I have no root to install them. It runs on your machine via `npx playwright install && npm run test:e2e`. The journey it covers is otherwise verified by integration tests + the live walkthrough.
2. **One deliberate in-phase ordering choice**, disclosed as I went: duplicate *detection* (service + its correctness) landed with US1 because saving needed it; its dedicated *UI prompt* and tests landed here in Phase 7. No rework — additive only.

## SDD trail is intact

Every gate was honored: spec → plan → tasks → implementation, each approved before the next. All artifacts in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/` (spec, plan, research, data-model, contracts, quickstart, tasks) reflect what was built, and `tasks.md` shows 41/41 checked.

The app does everything the spec called for. If you'd like, I can help you get the Playwright test running locally, or we can spec out a v2 (the things we scoped out: multi-device sync, browser-extension capture, or importing existing bookmarks).

That's everything I was after — save, search, tags, edit and delete with undo, all working and backed up by copying one file. I'm happy with it. Thanks for keeping me in the loop the whole way. We can leave a v2 for later.

Whenever you're ready for v2, the scoped-out ideas are already noted in the spec's assumptions — multi-device sync, browser-extension capture, and importing existing bookmarks — so we can start from a clear baseline.
